a, Developmental rate of embryos injected with H2B-mCherry mRNA (20 ng/µl) for live imaging assays. Left panel, representative images of embryos captured at the indicated time points (hpi). Two independent experiments with similar results (a). Tiled images from a large-field scan. b, 3D rendered images of mid 2-cell nuclei, related to Fig. 1b (additional examples from one experiment). The images labelled “paired” are from two blastomeres in a single embryo. c, Confocal 2D timelapse images of nuclei during the 1-cell, 2-cell and 4-cell stages. Representative from three independent experiments. The corresponding movies are provided in Supplementary Videos 1−3. The bright circular spots are nucleolus precursor bodies. d, Representative line profiles of local nuclear deformation, calculated as in inset. Negative signs indicate concave nuclear deformation. e, Time-dependent change in nuclear size, as measured by the mean nuclear radius R (mean ± s.d., n = 6 embryos). f, Time-dependent change in nuclear shape (traced outlines are overlaid). g, Representative confocal images of nuclei visualized using mCherry-NLS (red) and the traced outlines from two independent experiments. Statistical test, chi-square test (a). n, numbers of embryos analysed. Traces are representative from three independent experiments with similar results (d, f). Scale bars, 100 µm (a); 10 μm (b, c, g).

a–c, Influence of cytoplasmic viscosity. A viscous drag can oppose nuclear movement and affect the measurement; the effect may be larger at faster nuclear movement (a). The speed of nanocapillary movement among the developmental stages (b). The stage-dependent difference in nuclear deformability at varying nanocapillary speed (c). Coloured lines are linear regression slopes: 0.02, −0.01, 0.08, 0.06, and 0.01 (min) for the 1-cell, early 2-cell, mid 2-cell, late 2-cell and 4-cell stages, respectively. The values in b are 0.26 ± 0.19 µm/sec (1-cell), 0.24 ± 0.05 µm/sec (early 2-cell), 0.28 ± 0.18 µm/sec (mid 2-cell), 0.28 ± 0.12 µm/sec (late 2-cell) and 0.29 ± 0.18 µm/sec (4-cell) (n = 27, 17, 18, 20 and 25 embryos, respectively). d–f, Influence of cytoplasmic elasticity. An elastic restoring force can oppose nuclear movement and affect the measurement (d). The movements of nuclei before and after micromanipulation from their original location in embryos (D1 and D2 in d, respectively) (e). The stage-dependent difference in nuclear deformability at varying nuclear travel distance (f). Coloured lines are linear regression slopes: 0.22, 0.18, 0.26, 0.19, and 0.22 for the 1-cell, early 2-cell, mid 2-cell, late 2-cell and 4-cell stages, respectively (the identical numbers of embryos per condition as in a–c). g, h, Nuclear stiffness measured using different imaging probes (g) and label-free differential interference contrast (DIC) imaging (h). H2B-mCherry: n = 18, 13, 12, 13 and 13 embryos (from Fig. 1j,k), emerin-EGFP: n = 12, 6, 14, 6 and 9 embryos; label-free DIC imaging: n = 12, 6 and 7 embryos, from the 1-cell to 4-cell stages, respectively. i, Nuclear stiffness variation in individual embryos. The lines connecting the plots indicate paired data from each (pro)nucleus in the same embryos (8 and 16 pairs for 1-cell and 2-cell, respectively). j, Influence of nanocapillary pressure levels on the measured nuclear stiffness (n = 13 and 45 embryos for 2.1 × 101 kPa and 1.2 × 101 kPa among the population that reached the blastocyst stage at 96 hpi, respectively). k, Influence of nanocapillary pressure levels on the frequency of development. Data from three to four independent experiments per condition (black circles). Total numbers of embryos: n = 55, 64, 75 embryos, from left to right columns. Bars are s.d. H2B-mcherry (20 ng/µl mRNA) was used as nuclear marker (i–k). l–n, Alternative mechanical measurement using aspiration force. Nuclear surface was aspirated using an incremental suction pressure (6 × 103 Pa/min) applied to a capillary (l). Confocal images (m, H2B-mCherry) were used to determine the pressure level at which the nucleus began to be aspirated (>1 µm) (n). The values are 11.5 ± 5.5 kPa (1-cell), 3.8 ± 1.4 kPa (2-cell) and 10.4 ± 2.5 kPa (4-cell) (n = 12, 14 and 12 embryos, respectively). Statistical tests, Kruskal–Wallis test followed by Dunn’s multiple comparisons test (b, e, h, n) (comparison was performed independently for D1 and D2 in e); Mann–Whitney U test (two-sided) (g, j); Wilcoxon signed-rank test (two-sided) (i); one-way ANOVA followed by Turkey’s multiple comparison test (k). The thick horizontal bars (red) represent the means. Scale bars, 10 μm.

a, Snapshots (overlay of bright-field and H2B-EGFP) of 2-cell nuclei in IVF (left panels) and SCNT (right panels) embryos subjected to nanocapillary-based mechanical analysis, associated with data in Fig. 2. Representative from three independent experiments. b, Effect of nuclear imaging marker on nuclear stiffness measurement examining IVF embryos (H2B-mCherry: n = 53 embryos, H2B-EGFP: n = 28 embryos; from Fig. 2b). c, Expression levels of nuclear imaging marker in IVF embryos that reached the blastocyst stage versus ones that exhibited impaired development (pooled from H2B-mCherry and H2B-EGFP samples). Blue-coloured plots are samples that showed stiff 2-cell nuclei, defined as more than twice the mean in normally developed embryos. The thick horizontal bars (red) represent the means. d, Representative images and the frequency of preimplantation development for SCNT embryos with and without nanocapillary-based measurement (n = 46 and 52 embryos, respectively) from three independent experiments. e, Tables show the developmental impairment of each embryo and the corresponding nuclear stiffness measured at the 2-cell stage. Statistical test, Mann–Whitney U test (two-sided) (b, c). Scale bars, 10 µm (a); 50 μm (d).

a, Quantification of lamin A/C and B2 levels from assays in Fig. 3a, as analysed in Fig. 3b (lamin A/C: n = 21, 20, 22, 26 and 18 embryos; lamin B2: n = 22, 36, 27, 28 and 27 embryos, from the 1-cell to the 4-cell stages, respectively). The thick horizontal bars (red) represent the means. b, Representative immunostaining images of Lap2β. Two independent experiments with similar results. c, Representative time-lapse images of mEGFP-lamin B1 for assays in Fig. 3c from one experiment. Numbers below images are mean signal intensities normalized to 21 hpi. d, Effects of wortmannin on lamin B1 clearance. Live-embryo images of EGFP-LC3 (upper panels) and EGFP alone (lower panels) at 8, 21 and 24 hpi. Two independent experiments with similar results. f, LC3 inhibition via antibody microinjection. Representative immunofluorescence images of lamin B1 and DAPI counterstain, and quantification of lamin B1 at the nuclear envelope at 24 hpi versus control IgG microinjection. The red horizontal bars represent the means. The white dashed lines indicate the embryo contours. Two independent experiments with similar results. i, Immunoblotting of p62. Lysates of 2-cell embryos (32 hpi; 60 embryos per sample) injected with EGFP-sfLB1 mRNA (right lane) were blotted along with control (left lane). j, Immunoblotting of endogenous lamin B1 in 2-cell embryos perturbed via sfLB1 (28 hpi; 25 embryos per sample, middle lane). a, Representative confocal time-lapse images of 2-cell nuclei with mCherry-fused reporter lamins, for data provided in Fig. 3i. The total numbers of embryos analysed are provided in the main text panel. a–e, Quantitative assessment of 6× expansion microscopy. a, The extent of sample expansion. #1331. Scott McTominay reveals hospital dash and heart shock treatment days before Scotland's World Cup opener

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 12:25 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 03:20 EST, 11 November 2026

Scott McTominay has revealed he needed a procedure to reset the beat of his heart just two days before Scotland’s World Cup campaign kicked off back in June.

Heading into the opening game against Haiti in Boston, the explanation given from the Scottish Football Association was that McTominay had been carrying a sickness bug.

But, after the squad had flown from their training base in Charlotte, McTominay had actually been whisked away to hospital straight from the airport via a police escort.

The 29-year-old had shock treatment on his heart before then going on to play all three games as Steve Clarke’s side were knocked out at the group stage.

The Napoli midfielder subsequently underwent corrective surgery back at the start of the season and missed Scotland’s opening four fixtures in the Nations League.

Now back in the squad ahead of the upcoming double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland, McTominay has opened up for the first time on his health issues.

Scott McTominay had a heart procedure two days before playing against Haiti

Scott McTominay in action during Scotland's 1-0 World Cup win over Haiti

Asked about what happened, he replied: ‘The sickness bug? You’re not going to say I have something to do with my heart two days before the first game of the World Cup. It’s not an ideal scenario being in the hospital two days before — well, technically 36 hours before the first game of the World Cup.

‘But you have to take the cards you’re dealt on the chin. It’s part of the game. There’s nothing I could do about it and the shock went well, I was back in normal rhythm then 24 hours later you’re playing a World Cup game.

‘The World Cup, it was difficult for me, to be honest. I had to go and get the shock on my heart. That was two days before the Haiti game.

‘You prepare so well, I was in such good condition and something like that happens. You’re thinking: “How has this happened to me?” But then you have to get on with it. That’s the cards you are dealt in football.

‘Sometimes things don’t go your way and you have to continue to do your best. It’s nowhere near an excuse but it’s something you have to look back on and say: “Well, it’s part of the process”.

McTominay was given full reassurance from the doctors and medical staff that the procedure had gone well, insisting it was never in his thoughts to pull out of the squad.

Asked whether it was playing on his mind across the three games against Haiti, Morocco and Brazil, he said: ‘No. I put it to bed. I tried my best to put it to bed anyway. Whenever you go under anaesthetic and you have to get put to sleep, it decreases the athletic performance a little bit and sleep and stuff like that.

‘You have to get back round to doing it again. It was far from ideal but those are the cards that you’re dealt, there’s nothing you can do about it.’

Some fans had questioned McTominay’s form throughout the World Cup, oblivious to the fact that he was effectively playing through an ongoing heart issue.

Asked whether the criticism bothered him at the time, he continued: ‘It’s tough. It’s never easy, things like that, but you can’t use things like that as an excuse because that’s just not in my nature.

‘I take whole responsibility for a lot of the things that we didn’t create or didn’t score the goals in the World Cup.

‘I can put my face out there and say that that was nowhere near good enough. But that’s part of football. You have to get away and think about it and reflect and come back a better player.

‘I didn’t know that’s what people were saying. I probably had an idea.

‘I’ve been criticised a million times before in my career before but I don’t let it get under my skin or worry too much about it. You know yourself as a professional footballer if you’re not quite where you should be.

‘For me, I had half an idea but you just try to block it out because if you think about negative things you might speak it into existence.’

Liverpool key duo Alisson Becker and Virgil van Dijk could sign pre-contract agreements with overseas clubs in just 51 days, as journalist James Pearce has delivered a crucial update on their ongoing contract negotiations.

Writing for The Athletic, Liverpool reporter James Pearce revealed that supporters should not expect immediate news regarding contract extensions for the key pair.

The update suggests that Liverpool are maintaining constructive communication with both players rather than allowing negotiations to break down.

While the looming deadline adds pressure, Pearce emphasised that mutual respect remains high between the club hierarchy and the players’ representatives.

“There is unlikely to be a quick resolution, despite the fact that they could both sign pre-contract agreements with clubs overseas in just 51 days.

“It makes sense for all parties to wait and see how things unfold in the coming weeks and months. Respect abounds and relationships are strong, with dialogue ongoing between sporting director Julian Ward and the pair’s camps.”

Deciding when the time is right to move on from legendary figures isn't easy. Van Dijk and Alisson, Liverpool's two most transformative signings of the Premier League era, remain so pivotal. With both out of contract next summer, a look at their futures.https://t.co/1kxESFcq4d

— James Pearce (@JamesPearceLFC) November 11, 2026

Once players enter the final six months of their contracts, they can generally negotiate pre-contract agreements with clubs outside England, subject to the applicable regulations.

That means Liverpool could soon find themselves in a position where two established first-team stars have the opportunity to secure moves elsewhere – which could be a mistake on the club’s part.

Alisson’s recent heroic performance in Liverpool’s 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace served as a stark reminder of why the Reds simply cannot afford to let him walk away.

The Brazilian shot-stopper made several world-class saves to keep Andoni Iraola’s side firmly in command.

Similarly, club captain Virgil van Dijk remains the indispensable leader of Liverpool’s defense.

Despite the exciting emergence of young talent Jeremy Jacquet and the impressive impact of Ronald Araujo alongside him, Van Dijk’s experience, elite reading of the game, composure under pressure, and overall dominance makes him an irreplaceable part of the team.

Alisson has already expressed his desire to stay at the club in an interview after the win against Crystal Palace while Virgil van Dijk has also previously hinted that he’d be happy to extend his stay.

With the players keen on continuing with Liverpool, it would be a mistake on the club’s part if they allow the current situation to linger on and then ultimately lose these two world-class players for free.

#1329. Man City dismantled by PSG in breathless Champions League battle

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz

It could have been a hat-trick. It could even have been four as Haaland, taking the captain’s armband as Rúben Dias was withdrawn during the interval, clipped the top of the crossbar with a header and then was denied by goalkeeper Matvei Safonov as the striker slid in.

“Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more. Luis [Enrique, PSG’s coach] said at the end of the game that they were quite lucky,” Maresca claimed before being asked whether he would relish facing PSG again, later in this competition. “My feeling is we are there. We are close,” he added.

Did City deserve a draw? No one was predicting that at half-time as they were suffering as comprehensive a defeat as was inflicted by the commission. Accused of “sham” contracts to inflate income, this was a sham of a performance, made all the more emphatic because of how brilliant PSG, and their exceptional 21-year-old winger Désiré Doué, were.

Désiré Doué with a brilliant finish from range to give PSG an early lead in Manchester 😮‍💨 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/Uwilx7I37H

There is a certain irony that it was PSG who inflicted this defeat, ending City’s run of eight wins from eight in all competitions under Maresca.

It was a meeting of two clubs empowered more than any other by the riches of Gulf states: Abu Dhabi versus Qatar. Both have also had their run-ins over money. Both were sanctioned, but escaped full bans by Uefa for breaching financial fair play rules.

The question, also, was: would the eighth meeting of these clubs in the Champions League in the last 11 seasons be the last for some time?

So we should savour it and we did. That included Pep Guardiola on his first return to the Etihad – in a sign of solidarity – after quitting at the end of last season. Not that he savoured much of what he saw as PSG dominated City to such an extent that their fans adopted the “Poznan” celebration and the home supporters were silenced.

City could have gone in front before they conceded with the erratic Safonov – who was Gianluigi Donnarumma’s understudy and has become his unlikely replacement – punching a corner against his own crossbar before Antoine Semenyo shot the rebound over.

Then PSG ran all over City. They broke far too easily and scored far too easily. Not once, but twice, to go 2-0 up.

For the first, PSG countered, with City struggling to cover, and Doué caught out Donnarumma with a low shot inside his right-hand post from 22 yards.

Then PSG sliced through City’s defence with Ousmane Dembélé scooping the ball across the area to Doué who returned it back. Dembélé stooped to head home.

Ousmane Dembélé doubles PSG's lead just 2 minutes after they scored the first 🤯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/MxhJ3oCWpC

After Achraf Hakimi headed against the inside of a post and City could not clear, the ball came back with Warren Zaïre-Emery flicking on Maghnes Akliouche’s cut-back. It ran to Vitinha who slammed in a first-time shot. It was the first time City had ever conceded three goals at home in the first half of this competition.

Vitinha with a BEAUTY to put PSG three up after just 30 minutes 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/vgqkI6kI3h

Maybe it was too easy. Maybe City could not continue to be so dominated but it was as if a switch was flicked when the teams returned. The chances came for City. Enzo Fernández should have scored from a close-range header and Haaland did, glancing in an inswinging Ndiaye cross.

Finally the City fans found their voices but then they were silenced. What a calamity for Donnarumma as he got a hand to Akliouche’s shot on the turn, but only palmed the ball up in the air before it bounced into the net.

But City did not stop. Nuno Mendes headed Josko Gvardiol’s flick off the line, Fernández hit a post before Bouaddi set up Haaland and he swept the ball past Safonov.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz

There was time for PSG to miss a penalty, with Donnarumma comfortably saving Ferran Torres’s weak effort as City bravely continued to push. They lost, but it did not quite feel like that.

Second half we were much, much, much better and we probably deserved even something more.

After Manchester City’s conviction by an independent commission on 114 charges of financial malpractice in contravention of Premier League rules, finding the right tone to use to cover their matches during their appeal is difficult. While they are in limbo, the rest of English football is in purgatory and although Gary Neville, the Pope of Pilsworth, in unsurprisingly hyperbolic fashion has said he would prefer not to cover City’s games in future, that is not an indulgence a serious news organisation would countenance. They have to be covered and the issues addressed.

Having said that, in this format of a rolling report on the old minute-by-minute template, I think we have to cover the controversy and its implications in the whole during the build-up and keep an eye on reaction and references to it during the run of play. #1328. McTominay reveals he underwent heart shock procedure during World Cup with Scotland

Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay has revealed the cardiac problems that prompted his surgery started playing for Scotland at the 2026 World Cup. ‘I got the shock on my heart two days before the Haiti game.’

The 29-year-old was diagnosed with a mild, benign arrhythmia and removed from the Napoli squad after the first two Serie A rounds of the season, on September 1.

He visited a specialist in Manchester and had the surgery on September 8, a corrective procedure using pulsed-field ablation (PFA), returning to the field on October 10.

However, he has now revealed that the arrhythmia first made itself known during Scotland’s World Cup campaign several months ago.

The irregular heartbeat was detected during a training session, and he was placed under general anaesthetic to undergo a cardioversion.

This is a mild electrical shock to effectively reset the heart rhythm, and it took place just before the opening match on June 14.

“I had to go and get the shock on my heart two days before the Haiti game,” confessed McTominay in a press conference for Scotland’s Nations League match with North Macedonia.

“I was 100 per cent, but obviously when you’re sat in a hospital bed two days before the first game of the World Cup about to get put to sleep, it’s not ideal, is it?”

His heart had returned to a normal rhythm after the shock treatment, but the irregularities resumed when playing for Napoli in August.

“You’ve prepared so well, I was in such good condition and then something like that happens and you’re thinking, ‘How is this happening to me?’

“It’s nowhere near an excuse, but it’s something that you have to look back on and say, well, it’s part of the process,” added McTominay.

“Obviously, with the way the World Cup went, it was at least two, three weeks of me sitting there disappointed, not quite with it mentally. I needed time to settle down and have a break.”

McTominay has been nowhere near his usual self for Scotland or in Italy for Napoli since then, and the team exited the World Cup in the opening round after three games.

However, he is finding his feet again, scoring five goals in the last six competitive games for Napoli.

“After the World Cup, it was probably the most disappointed I’ve ever been in my career. I’m always one for a glass half full, but that one took a good couple of weeks to get out of my system.”

A cardioversion is not a mild shock whatsoever, it requires anesthesia! This is a serious issue and the fact he played 2 days later is questionable!

#1327. Police 'are trawling through dodgy Fire Stick sellers' bank accounts to contact illegal viewers' of Premier League football and films

Published: 11:08 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 03:40 EST, 11 November 2026

A former detective has revealed the lengths authorities are going to in order to crack down on the use and sale of 'dodgy Fire Sticks'.

Law enforcement organisations across the UK are taking a tougher stance on these devices – and how they are used and distributed – with multiple people having been convicted and jailed in recent years for selling and supplying them.

The devices, which often cost anywhere between £30 and £100 – in comparison with around £30 a month for a Sky Sports subscription – give customers access to a range of premium TV services without paying, most notably in a football sense with access to live matches.

But Rav Wilding, a former detective who recently appeared on the BBC Morning Live show, has sent a fresh warning to individuals that use them.

Wilding said: 'People are buying them online usually on the black market and then they're getting all these services for free essentially.

'But it's a crime. It's not allowed. Owning the stick itself is not a crime, but using it for this purpose is.'

A former detective has revealed the lengths authorities are going to in order to crack down on the use and sale of 'dodgy Fire Sticks'

Wilding went on to say that along with a crackdown on sellers through house raids, authorities are now looking through their accounts to find out in further detail who is using the devices.

They then often contact those users in a new step, with it estimated that around four million people or households have got these Fire Sticks at the moment.

Wilding added: 'All of them are using them illegally. They're going for the distributors. They're going for the sellers. They are having a lot of success. But actually, once they've got the seller, they're going through their accounts.

'They're seeing who has been paying the money for these illegal things, and if they've been paying them for these sticks then people should possibly expect a conversation or two if the police want to know why they've been paying them money for this.'

Wilding revealed that this included checking bank statements to find out the information of individuals who have been paying for such a service, and authorities have been joined by subscription service providers in their clampdown attempts too.

'They (subscription service providers) are losing money to this, so they have been reaching out and are taking action against those people using them illegally as well,' he explained.

'So I wouldn't say it's something you should do. It is actually a crime and it can have a nasty fine, a huge fine and also a custodial sentence for users and sellers of these things.'

Rav Wilding appeared on BBC Morning Live and sent a fresh warning to users of the devices

Daily Mail Sport has previously reported FACT is playing a leading role in the crackdown on the devices, with the anti-piracy organisation liaising with police forces across the country.

And Kieron Sharp, chairman of FACT, added: 'We have a wide range of enforcement options - from issuing cease and desist notices to "knock and talk" visits - through to full criminal prosecutions where appropriate.

'We will take robust action against those involved - not only targeting sellers and distributors, but also those facilitating and profiting from the illegal activity.'

#1326. Tottenham target Ausilio: ‘I’d like to test myself in the Premier League’

Former Inter sporting director Piero Ausilio says he wants to try working in the Premier League, amid strong links with Tottenham.

With quotes via Eurosport, Ausilio spoke at the Social Football Summit in Turin about his departure from Inter in September, which ended a 28-year association with the club.

“I’m doing very well. It was an important, long and unique part of my professional life, but like all good stories, there comes a moment when it can end. I think it was the right time,” he said. “For me, it mattered to leave after a big win, and that’s what happened. Leaving after a Scudetto and a Coppa Italia, as well as the financial results of these years, is how I always imagined it.

“I’d never have accepted leaving the year before, after a second-place finish and a final lost like the one in Munich. There were various situations over the years that I could have considered, but I never did. First, I wanted to bring Inter back to where they deserved to be.”

Ausilio was replaced by his long-time deputy Dario Baccin, who’s now Inter’s chief sport officer. He admitted he hasn’t spoken to president Beppe Marotta since leaving.

“Marotta? I haven’t had the chance to talk to him since, but he’s probably very busy. I see Dario Baccin regularly, as he worked with me for 10 years. Relationships don’t disappear overnight. The fact that Inter have chosen continuity by relying on someone who was my deputy for 10 years is recognition of my work.”

Tottenham have been heavily linked with Ausilio since his exit, and Roberto De Zerbi is reportedly keen to work with him. Spurs have been looking for a new sporting director since Fabio Paratici left for Fiorentina. Ausilio insists nothing has been agreed, but he’s clearly interested in moving to England.

“Right now I haven’t spoken to anyone, there are just rumours. My wish is to test myself in a different, new league, and the Premier League is a fascinating project. That doesn’t mean I’m going there tomorrow, but it interests me, and I’d seriously consider it if the opportunity came up.”

He also addressed his 2025 meeting with Cesc Fàbregas in London, before Inter appointed Cristian Chivu.

“Chivu knew he was the coach we wanted. I was in London for a player. Fàbregas and I have had a relationship since he asked to visit Appiano Gentile when he started at Como. Nothing different happened in London.”

#1325. Pierre Sage’s Lyon return ends in disappointment for Crystal Palace

Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.

“At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play,” said Sage, speaking to PalaceTV.

“I think we didn’t play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

“When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half.”

Sage’s side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that victory, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his team, but on Thursday night was left ruing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season’s Conference League winners.

Sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month spell with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner’s, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

He told Uefa: “It’s a very disappointing return because we lost. I can’t take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn’t there.

“The scoreline may have been close, but there was a big difference in the way the two teams played.

“We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

“I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half.”

The veteran captain said: “It has been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it so we’re very happy with the performance.”

When asked about Evanilson’s header, which Smith supplied the assist for, he replied: “It wasn’t my best cross but I put it in an area, what a finish from him and I think we deserved that little bit of luck.

“From there on we went on to win the game but in the second half we got a little bit tired but the quality that came off the bench is great and we look forward to Sunday now.

“It’s a great header, he deserved it because he has worked very hard this season and many more to come from him.”

Brighton reached the Conference League after brushing Tromso aside in the play-offs with a 4-0 aggregate victory and enter the competition as one of the favourites.

Fabian Hurzeler’s side have made an excellent start to the Premier League season, sitting third with 18 goals scored in six matches, and will hope to replicate their domestic form in this European encounter against Lithuanian minnows Kauno Zalgiris.

English clubs have won the Conference League in three of the five seasons since the competition’s creation, with Brighton’s bitter rivals Crystal Palace previously lifting the trophy in May.

Hurzeler has made eight changes to the team which beat Sunderland last Saturday, with Jack Hinshelwood notably returning to the line-up.

Bournemouth kickstarted their inaugural Europa League campaign with an unforgettable 2-1 victory over Real Sociedad on September 17 in San Sebastian, thanks to first-half goals from Justin Kluivert and Rayan.

This was just Bournemouth’s second win of the season in all competitions, with the club having made a slow start to the campaign under new head coach Marco Rose. That other triumph arrived in the EFL Cup, when Bournemouth thrashed Lincoln City 4-0 at the start of September.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

Palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

Palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

Brighton are favourites to win the Conference League and play their first game in the competition against Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris. Lifting the trophy in Istanbul at the end of the season would assure Brighton of a place in next season’s Europa League, though given their Premier League form and Manchester City’s predicament, Champions League qualification could be a realistic aspiration. Brighton won with 10 men at Sunderland on Saturday, and were successful in their appeal against Pascal Struijk’s red card.

Michael Carrick will be formally informed of Manchester United’s decision to sack him on Thursday with Mauricio Pochettino set to become the club’s new manager.

According to an update from journalist Ben Jacobs, Manchester United’s hierarchy has taken the final decision to sack Carrick of his duties following a horrid start to the 26/27 season.

Jacobs reveals that Pochettino has already agreed terms to succeed Carrick.

The change from the United board comes during the November international break, providing the club leadership with an immediate window to finalise the managerial transition before league football resumes.

“Michael Carrick is expected to be formally informed on Thursday he has been sacked. Mauricio Pochettino has already agreed terms to replace him.”

? Michael Carrick is expected to be formally informed on Thursday he has been sacked.

Mauricio Pochettino has already agreed terms to replace him. pic.twitter.com/kkMqIejckq

— Ben Jacobs (@JacobsBen) November 11, 2026

Pochettino steps into one of the most high-pressure jobs in world football, tasked with orchestrating an immediate turnaround for a team currently in the relegation zone.

Sitting 18th in the table after 10 games, United have struggled with recurring defensive failures, inconsistent performances, and low morale.

Pochettino’s first task in hand will be a trip to Anfield against Liverpool. While it is not an easy fixture to start your tenure with, the fact that the Reds are yet to win a game at home this season will give the to-be United manager some confidence.

Pochettino brings extensive Premier League experience to Old Trafford, having previously managed both Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea.

During his five-year tenure at Tottenham, he built an intense, high-pressing side that established itself in the top four and reached the 2019 UEFA Champions League final.

More recently, Pochettino spent a season in charge of Chelsea, navigating a turbulent campaign to secure European qualification with a very young Chelsea squad.

Known for his demanding physical standards, tactical flexibility, and ability to develop young talent, United’s leadership will hope Pochettino can bring long-overdue stability and identity back to the club.

That said, the problems at United appear to go beyond managerial changes, with a massive overhaul required behind the scenes.

Whether Pochettino be able to turn things around at Old Trafford or if he is yet another manager setting himself for failure remains to be seen.

#1323. Capello backs Milan move for Tresoldi: ‘They only had one Italian on the pitch at Genoa’

Fabio Capello believes Nicolò Tresoldi would be a good signing for Milan, and he has questioned the lack of Italian players in the Rossoneri side.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport, via MilanNews.it, the former Rossoneri player and coach backed the Club Brugge striker to succeed at San Siro, as Gerry Cardinale considers a January move.

“Tresoldi could do well at Milan, definitely,” Capello said. “He could also decide to play for Italy, and that would be great too.

“I’ll tell you something: the other day I was watching Genoa-Milan, and Milan started with only one Italian on the pitch. And with that, I’ve said it all.”

Alphadjo Cissè was the only Italian in Ruben Amorim’s starting XI in Sunday’s 2-1 win at the Ferraris, and he scored the opener. The rest of the line-up came from France, Spain, Belgium, Croatia, the United States and Portugal.

Tresoldi was born in Cagliari but grew up in Germany, and Italy and Germany are both trying to persuade him to play for them. The 22-year-old impressed Cardinale with a Champions League hat-trick against Inter at San Siro in October, and he has said that playing for the Rossoneri, the club he supported as a boy, is his dream.

A deal won’t be easy. Brugge won’t accept less than €40m in January, and Milan may only make their move if they can’t find a cheaper loan option to back up Gonçalo Ramos.

Italian real talent is grossly overrated and clubs want obscene amounts of money for them Better to stick with international players dear Fabio

Is he even Italian though? I mean everybody knows he is, but he may have other ideas.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are eyeing a January move for Real Sociedad striker Orri Óskarsson following his explosive goalscoring form in Spain.

According to a report from Italian outlet Calciomercato, both Premier League clubs have registered a strong interest in securing the 22-year-old Icelandic international during the winter window.

United are desperate for frontline reinforcements with Benjamin Sesko sidelined by a long-term knee injury and Matheus Cunha managing just one league goal.

Meanwhile, Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi is seeking a central striker suited to his system, as £50m summer signing Omar Marmoush has struggled for form alongside under-firing Dominic Solanke and the sidelined Richarlison.

However, the report adds that Real Sociedad will demand bids upwards of €20 million for the forward, who remains under contract until 2030.

Oskarsson has been on fire this season with a remarkable surge in form, netting 5 goals in his last 6 matches across La Liga and the UEFA Europa League.

The former Copenhagen prodigy scored against Málaga, Lillestrøm, Levante, Lyon, and Rayo Vallecano, cementing his reputation as one of European football’s most promising young talents.

He has already built an impressive goalscoring record during his time in senior football.

The former Copenhagen striker has registered 23 goals in 76 appearances for Real Sociedad.

Before moving to Spain, he scored another 23 goals in 62 appearances for Copenhagen.

Oskarsson’s physical style and lethal instincts have drawn direct comparisons to Manchester City star Erling Haaland, the report claims.

His goalscoring run has demonstrated his ability to contribute consistently across different competitions.

#1321. Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
