(a) Tumors 4 and 7 analyzed as in Fig. 1h. Cells are colored by classification or the indicated feature levels. (b) Heatmap of mean feature levels in each subpopulation across all HR+ tumors analyzed by CyTOF (n = 14, including 3 anchor repeats, see Table S3). Rows present standardized values. (c) Two luminal PDX models analyzed by CyTOF after removal of mouse cells (human CD298-positive; mouse MHC class 1-negative), and classification into three subpopulations (Fig. 1j). PDX-1 comprised of six tumors, with equal cell sampling per tumor; PDX-2 comprised of one tumor. Heatmaps show the mean feature levels within each subpopulation for each model. (d) UMAP of MCF7 CyTOF data using all measured markers. Points are colored by cluster (left) or the indicated feature or signature (right).

(a) Distribution of DBSACN-defined cell subpopulations across independent MCF7 CyTOF experiments of MCF7 cells, showing consistent proportions of the different cell states. (b) UMAP representation and DBSCAN clustering of two different MCF7 parental cells or single-cell derived clones analyzed by CyTOF, using only epigenetic features. Points are colored by the classification of different subpopulations or the expression levels of the indicated feature or signature (PermCell). (c) The distribution of cells among the populations defined by DBSCAN clustering in the MCF7 parental (p) or single-cell derived clones (c). The single-cell derived clones recapitulate the entire spectrum of heterogeneity observed in the parental population. (d) UMAP representation of CyTOF analysis of six independently grown tumors from the PDX-1 model (n = 6 tumors, each grown in a different mouse), colored by subpopulations. Cells from each individual tumor are mapped onto the joint UMAP, and the distribution of cells among the three subpopulations for each tumor is shown.

(a) Confusion matrix of XGBoost model predictions for all 3 subpopulations across HR+ tumors (n = 14) using only epigenetic features, excluding cell identity markers. Rows were normalized to show predictions as percentages of cells within each true class. (b) Representative examples of XGBoost-based noise prediction procedure. UMAPs of individual tumors are shown before (left) and after (right) prediction. Points are colored by classification; non-clustered cells before prediction, or cells in which prediction confidence <95% are marked in gray. (c-d) XGBoost models distinguishing Cycling cells from all other tumor cells (c) or specifically the basal-like cells (d) within the HR+ CyTOF cohort. SHAP scores show feature contributions to classification, ranked in descending order. (e) Percentage of proliferating cells (assessed by the levels of pRb, as in Fig. S3) in each epigenetic sub-populations (Cycling, luminal and basal-like). The basal-like and luminal sub-populations do not differ due to differences in the proliferative state. (f) The differences in the average levels of the indicated features between the basal-like and luminal sub-populations in the luminal PDX models. Basal-like cells show a recurrent pattern of both up and downregulated histone PTMs, highly similar to the pattern observed in fresh human tumors.

(a) UMAP of CyTOF data from tumors (as in Fig. S4), colored by the assigned clusters (top) or the basal-like epigenetic signature (basal PermCell score, bottom), which is derived solely from histone modifications. (b) UMAP of two MCF7 parental cultures and three single-cell-derived clones analyzed by CyTOF using only epigenetic features, colored by assigned clusters (top) or the basal-like epigenetic signature (bottom).

(a) Scatter plot comparing basal-like cell fraction with estrogen receptor (ER) positivity by IHC across tumors (n = 11). Spearman correlation coefficient and two-sided p-value are indicated. (b,c) Basal-like cell fraction in HR+ tumors stratified by progesterone receptor (PR) IHC (b; 100% PR-positive, n = 7; lower PR positivity, n = 4) or TP53 status (c; wild-type, n = 8; mutant, n = 3). Two-sided Wilcoxon tests. Boxes show median and 25th–75th percentiles; whiskers extend within 1.5xIQR. (d) Differential protein abundance between K5High and K5Low populations in tumor 19. Axes show protein intensity difference (K5High-K5Low) and -log10(p-value), respectively. Two-sided Student’s t-tests with FDR correction; Green and pink dots depict proteins significantly deregulated (Fold change>1.5, q-value < 0.05). Labeled are chromatin regulators differentially expressed between the two populations. (e) Principal component analysis (PCA) of RNA-seq profiles from sorted MCF7 subpopulations. Basal-like cells (K5High GATA3Low, n = 3), extreme luminal cells (K5Low GATA3High, n = 3), and bulk MCF7 cells (n = 2). Points represent independently sorted population. Axes indicate variance explained. (f) Differential gene expression between basal-like (K5High GATA3Low, n = 3) and bulk MCF7 cells (n = 2). Significantly upregulated (pink) and downregulated (green) genes are indicated (DESeq2, Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted p-value < 0.05, log2FC > 1). EMT-associated genes (hallmark epithelial-mesenchymal transition gene set) are enriched among upregulated transcripts in the basal-like population and highlighted with a black outline. CD74, a membrane-bound protein upregulated in the basal-like cells, is marked in dark pink. (g) CD74 expression across basal-like (n = 3), bulk (n = 2), and extreme luminal (n = 3) MCF7 populations. Points represent independently sorted population; expression is shown as rld values. Statistical significance was derived from DESeq2 differential expression analysis with Benjamini–Hochberg correction for multiple testing. (h) Representative wound-healing assay images of sorted CD74Low and CD74High MCF7 cells at the indicated times. Three independently recovered sorted populations from the same sort were analyzed. The gap area is highlighted in green. Scale bar = 300 μm.

(a) TCGA-BRCA DNA-methylation dataset (n = 782)51 was deconvoluted into three archetypes. Dots show tumor archetype composition and colored by PAM50 subtype. The archetype V3 is associated with basal-like triple-negative tumors. The composition of archetypes within the three tumors analyzed in this study (T18, T19, and T23, highlighted) clusters with luminal breast tumors from the TCGA cohort. (b) Genes were ranked by correlation between methylation archetypes and matched TCGA-BRCA expression, followed by GSEA111 against MSigDB hallmark gene sets (Table S4b). V1 and V2 archetypes are associated with luminal transcriptional programs while V3 archetype is enriched for the EMT program. Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) of representative terms are shown. Black outline denotes BH-adjusted p-value < 0.05. See Fig. S5a for all terms. (c-d) K5High and K5Low sorted cells from tumors 5 and 23 were subjected to enzyme-mediated methylation sequencing (EM-seq, n = 4 replicates, 200 cells/replicate), and differentially methylated gene promoters were identified. For each sample, functional enrichment analysis was performed separately for genes with hypermethylated or hypomethylated promoters. Shown are the top 10 enriched terms from the MSigDB Hallmark gene set collection (c) or a curated list of breast cancer cell identity signatures (d) with nominal p-value < 0.05 (one-sided hypergeometric test). Circle size represents the number of genes from the input list overlapping each gene set, and transparency reflects -log10(p-value). (e) A CpG-island (CGI) methylation signature distinguishing K5High and K5Low states, derived using CGIs showing concordant differential methylation between the states in both tumor 5 and 23. Shown is the projection of this signature into DNA methylation profiles from the TCGA-BRCA dataset. Positive scores indicate greater similarity to the EM-seq-derived K5High methylation program, whereas negative scores indicate similarity to the K5Low state. Boxplots show the distribution of signature scores across basal-like (n = 96) or luminal (n = 418) tumors with points representing individual tumors. Boxes show median and 25th–75th percentiles; whiskers extend to the largest/smallest value within 1.5×IQR. The K5High methylation program is enriched in basal-like breast tumors. Two-sided Mann–Whitney U test. (f) TCGA-BRCA DNA-methylation dataset deconvoluted into three archetypes as in a, with K5high and K5low-sorted populations from tumors 5 and 23 projected onto the archetype space. K5high populations are shifted toward the V3 archetype, consistent with enrichment for basal/EMT-associated methylation programs. (g) Representation of tumors from the TCGA-BRCA cohort based on the four-archetype decomposition described in Fig. 3a, colored by V1 contribution. K5high and K5low-sorted populations from tumors 5 and 23 are projected onto the UMAP embedding. K5high populations are localized to regions characterized by higher V1 contribution, consistent with the EMT-associated methylation programs.

(a) WGBS reads were clustered by DNA methylation patterns over 100 bp bins55, and each bin was scored for entropy, reflecting DNA methylation pattern heterogeneity; bins containing one pattern have zero entropy. Illustration, rows represent methylation patterns, filled/open circles indicate methylated/unmethylated CpGs and #r denotes supporting reads. Histograms show mean entropy scores of CGIs in tumor 19 (n = 17,434), tumor 18 (n = 20,845) and tumor 23 (n = 22,440). Most CGIs are unmethylated and have zero entropy scores. The intermediate and high-entropy bins are marked in pink and red. (b) Intermediate- and high-entropy CGIs (entropy>0) were linked to genes and analyzed for enrichment against MSigDB Hallmark genesets85. Pathways significantly enriched in all three tumors are shown (one-sided hypergeometric test, nominal p-value < 0.05). Dot size indicates overlapping genes; color indicates -log10(p-value). Variable CGIs are significantly enriched for genes related to EMT. (c) The Basal-luminal index was used to score the transcriptional identity of tumor cells13, and cells from each tumor were divided into quartiles; a low index score corresponds to expression of luminal identity genes (Q1) and a high index score corresponds to expression of basal-like identity genes (Q4). Cell-to-cell distance was calculated within each quartile to assess transcriptional heterogeneity; medians are shown for each sample. Bottom, representative UMAP and quartile definition for tumor 12-R. (d) Vendi score96 was used to calculate epigenetic heterogeneity within luminal or basal-like subpopulation (as defined in Figs. 1, 2, across n = 11 luminal tumors) using single-cell CyTOF histone PTMs measurements. Points show the mean across 5,000 rarefactions; error bars indicate uncertainty intervals (2.5th–97.5th percentiles) of the rarefied score distribution. Histone PTM levels are more variable in basal-like cells.

(a) UMAPs of H3K4me1 (left, n = 17,062 cells) and H3K4me3 (right, n = 12,883 cells) snCUT&Tag 50 kb bins matrices from three tumor samples (PC1 representing read counts excluded; CD45-negative cells). Shared stroma clusters are outlined. (b) UMAPs as in a, colored according to H3K4me1 or H3K4me3 enrichment over fibroblast identity genes: FAP, COL3A1 and DCN (left) or endothelial identity genes: EMCN, PECAM1 and NOTCH3 (right). Higher UCell scores indicate stronger enrichment at genes associated with the corresponding stromal identity. (c,d) H3K4me1 (c) or H3K4me3 (d) UMAPS from all three tumors (50k bins matrix), colored by cluster. The portion of cells from each tumor that constitutes the clusters is shown below. Shared clusters were classified as stroma, as verified by gene activity; Boxed tumor clusters were analyzed further. For H3K4me3, limited number of cells passed quality control thresholds for tumor 8, thus data quality for this sample is lower. (e) Genomic annotation of H3K4me1 and H3K4me3 snCUT&Tag pseudo-bulk peaks, after stoma removal. Stacked bar plots show percentage of peaks assigned to genomic features. (f) For each tumor sample, removing the stroma compartment, a scTransform-normalized H3K4me3 gene activity was generated (excluding read counts information), represented by UMAP and clustered using Louvain clustering. Cell numbers are indicated. (g) Tumor 8 H3K4me1 UMAP (Fig. 3e), colored by UCell scores derived based on the genes contributing to the enrichment of the indicated terms. Cluster 2 shows high H3K4me1 signal on genes associated with basal-like cell identity. While the EMT signature was not significantly enriched for this cluster (FDR-adjusted p-value > 0.05), the corresponding UCell score is shown for comparison using EMT-associated genes contributing to the cluster. (h) Differentially H3K4me3-bound genes identified for each cluster shown in f (two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, log2FC > 1, adjusted p-value < 0.01) were tested against MSigDB Hallmark and Breast-related genesets (Table S4). Terms enriched in cluster 1 in all three tumors are shown (one-sided hypergeometric test, FDR-adjusted P < 0.05). (i) Pseudu-bulk H3K4me1 and H3K4me3 genome-browser tracks from basal-like clusters (pink) or equal numbers of cells sampled from all other clusters (green) at representative genomic regions.

(a,b) H3K4me1 or H3K4me3 reads per cell versus negative ER-signaling score in tumor 15 (a) or positive ER-signaling score in tumor 18 (b). Points represent cells; r is Pearson’s correlation coefficient. (c) H3K4me1 snCUT&Tag UMAPs from tumors 15 and 18 (Fig. 3e), colored by CyTOF-derived labels (top), with predicted-label composition per snCUT&Tag cluster (middle) and UCell scores for the ‘Down in Luminal vs. Basal (Charafe)’ signature (bottom). (d) Cells were classified as luminal or basal-like by CyTOF label transfer as in c. Differences in mean UCell scores for the indicated signatures between basal-like and luminal cells are shown across three tumors. EMT and basal-like-associated gene signatures show higher H3K4me1 deposition in the CyTOF-predicted basal-like group. (e) K5High and K5Low sorted cell populations from the luminal PDX model or MCF7 cells were subjected to H3K4me1 CUT&Tag. Peaks unique to each population were assigned to genes and compared to the indicated gene signatures. Shown is the difference in the GeneRatio (overlap count divided by the total number of peak-associated genes in that population) for each population, with positive values indicating increased overlap in K5High (basal-like) cells, whereas negative values indicate increased overlap in K5Low (luminal) cells. (f) Tumor 8 H3K9me2 snCUT&Tag UMAP from a 20kb-bin matrix, clustered by Leiden clustering (left). Stroma percentages per cluster, based on the H3K4me1-trained classifier, are shown on the right. (g) Following removal of the stromal compartment described in f, a normalized promoter-proximal H3K9me2 occupancy matrix was generated, and Leiden clustering was applied (n = 4,419 cells, see Methods). (h) Percentage of basal-like cells (cluster 2 in Fig. 3e) within each cluster in g, based on the H3K4me1-trained classifier. (i) Left: Differentially H3K9me2-bound genes in cluster 4, shown in g (two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, log2FC > 0.6, adjusted p-value < 0.01), were tested against MSigDB Hallmark and Breast-related signatures. Shown are the top 5 terms significantly enriched (nominal p-value < 0.05) for genes with upregulation of H3K9me2 on their promoters. Right: UMAP as in g colored according to UCell gene-signature scores for the indicated gene sets. Cluster 4 shows elevated H3K9me2 occupancy over luminal-associated genes. (j) Read count per cell (nCount) by cluster (panel g). Violin plots show the distribution of individual cells, with the median denoted by a white dot and n indicated for each cluster. Cluster 4 shows the highest number of reads per cell, possibly corresponding to higher global levels of this mark in basal-like cells.

(a,b) Classifier performance in an independently processed, batch-corrected cohort of healthy individuals (n = 19) and luminal BC patients (n = 30), using the model trained on the original cohort in Fig. 4f. (a) ROC curve (AUC = 0.98; shading, 95% CI). (b) Confusion matrix with specificity set to 0.9. (c,d) ROC curve discriminating healthy individuals (n = 32) from luminal BC patients, diagnosed at the SHEBA medical center, Israel (c, n = 16, AUC = 0.96) or Kaplan medical center, Israel (d, n = 14, AUC = 0.99). Shading indicates the 95% CI. (e) ROC curve discriminating healthy individuals (n = 32) and triple-negative BC patients (n = 22, AUC = 0.98, shading indicates the 95% CI). (f) Healthy (n = 51) and luminal BC samples from three medical centers (n = 137) were pooled and stratified into 75% training cohort and a 25% test cohort. ROC curves are shown for training (left, n = 38 healthy vs. 103 luminal BC samples, AUC = 0.96) and the test cohort (right, n = 13 healthy vs. 34 luminal BC patients, AUC = 0.94). Shading indicates the 95% CI. (g) AUC estimates for discrimination of healthy individuals (n = 51) from luminal A (n = 98), luminal B (n = 31), or all luminal BC patients (n = 137) across the three medical centers. Points and lines indicate AUCs and 95% CIs, respectively.

(a-f) Selected EPINUC features in disease-free versus recurrent-disease groups within clinically defined subsets (see Fig. 5a): >50% ER-positive (a, n = 39 vs. 28), >50% PR-positive (b, n = 33 vs. 18), luminal A BC (c, n = 35 vs. 23), T1-T2 staged tumors (d, n = 43 vs. 20), grade 1-2 tumors (e, n = 36 vs. 18), and no LVI at diagnosis (f, n = 34 vs. 14). Two-sided Wilcoxon tests. (g) Distribution of 29 EPINUC features across luminal BC patients stratified by histological grade (grade 1, n = 29; grade 2, n = 67; grade 3, n = 36). Points represent individual patients. Kruskal-Wallis p-values were Benjamini-Hochberg-corrected across the 29 features. (h) Spearman correlations between mean histone PTM levels measured by CyTOF in tumor cells and EPINUC measurements in matched plasma (n = 10). Correlations with r > 0.2 are pink; P < 0.05 is bold (two-sided Spearman correlation test). H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 scatter plots are shown below, with Theil-Sen fits and 95% CIs. (i) Individual PPS analysis distinguishing disease-free (DF) from relapse (R, left column), or between healthy individuals (H) and each of the luminal outcome group. Color indicates PPS, reflecting predictive power of each individual feature. (j) OncotypeDX scores for patients in cohorts MAYO-1 and MAYO-2 with available measurements (disease-free, n = 40; relapse, n = 9, n.s., non-significant, two-sided Wilcoxon test). In a–g,j, boxes show median and 25th–75th percentiles; whiskers extend to the largest/smallest value within 1.5×IQR.

#1276. Pio Esposito impressed Upamecano ahead of Italy vs. France

France international Dayot Upamecano is impressed by Italy striker Francesco Pio Esposito, noting it is ‘not easy to mark him,’ but won’t change his style for this Nations League clash.

It kicks off at San Siro on Thursday at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

This is the penultimate round of the group stage, with France leading on 10 points, followed by Italy with seven and Belgium on six.

In Matchday 6, France will host rock bottom Turkiye, while it is a head-to-head between the Azzurri and Red Devils in Brussels on Sunday.

“Italy are a very good team, they changed coach and have players at top clubs,” said Upamecano in his press conference.

“Our concentration is always the same, we are focused entirely on doing well for France. There is no reason to change our style of play, we want to replicate what we do in training, and hope to do so tomorrow.”

France have dropped points only once in this Nations League campaign, in the 1-1 draw with Italy in Paris on October 2.

Inter striker Pio Esposito started that match and he is expected to lead the attack again tomorrow evening.

“Esposito is a very good player, very physical, we saw in the first match it was not easy to mark him. I would prefer not to concentrate on a single player, though, because we are taking on the whole Italy team,” noted Upamecano.

It was not an easy match for Upamecano, who was sent off for a second bookable offence against Italy.

“France try to keep a high defensive line, to press and recover the ball quickly. I like this style of play, and we’ll try to keep that going tomorrow against Italy.”

Like the first leg in Paris, France are again without injured Kylian Mbappé, while Marcus Thuram, Esteban Lepaul, Ousmane Dembélé, Aurelien Tchouameni, Manu Koné and Pierre Kalulu are also among those who withdrew from the squad.

“It’s true, we are missing a lot of players and I wish them all a speedy recovery, but we are still ready to face Italy, that goes for all those who start and can come off the bench.”

Jeremy Jacquet has been tipped to step into the defence with Upamecano in a reshuffle tomorrow.

“I don’t know, you’d have to ask Zidane. He is a young lad, very motivated, and we hope he can keep going like this.”

The Bayern Munich full-back was asked if he would like to play in the Premier League in future.

“I’ve lived in Germany for a while and I am happy there. We’ll see what happens in future, but I am happy at Bayern Munich,” he replied.

“I am always ready to improve, try to listen to the advice I receive, and give my all. I think there’s a lot that I can do better.”

#1275. Barcelona rout Alavés 6-1 to retake LaLiga lead before top-two clash with Atlético

Barcelona beat Alavés 6-1 at Spotify Camp Nou to go back to the top of LaLiga. The win came with a reshuffled defence and sets up a meeting of the top two at the Metropolitano.

Atlético Madrid had gone top of LaLiga earlier on 31 October by winning at Levante. Within hours, Barcelona took the place back. Hansi Flick’s side dismantled Alavés in front of their own fans. The result ended a two-game losing run after defeats to PSG and Real Madrid.

Barcelona have scored 46 goals and conceded 12, a goal difference of +34, according to the official LaLiga table. Atlético have scored 22 and conceded 8.

This was Barcelona’s first test since the Clásico. Real Madrid won that game 2-1 at Camp Nou on 25 October. Kylian Mbappé scored twice, the second in the 87th minute, after Raphinha had equalised on 61 minutes. That defeat ended a run of nine straight league wins at the start of the season.

Raphinha opened the scoring in the 8th minute. Fermín López added a second in the 23rd. Raphinha struck again in the 41st, and Lamine Yamal made it four in first-half stoppage time. Barcelona held 77% of the ball, in front of a crowd of 53,523.

Yamal’s second goal, in the 64th minute, was first ruled out for offside. A VAR review showed his run was onside. He was taken off to a standing ovation soon afterwards, with Gordon replacing him.

The former Newcastle winger scored in the 81st minute, his first league goal for the club. He ran on to a through ball from Rodri and chipped the goalkeeper. Mariano Díaz pulled one back for Alavés in the 84th minute.

Absences left Flick short at the back. Fariñas started at right-back and played the full 90 minutes. Frenkie de Jong moved to centre-back alongside Cubarsí. João Cancelo completed the back four at left-back. Gerard Martín replaced De Jong in the 82nd minute.

Fariñas is normally a midfielder. He is from the Valencian Community and joined Barcelona as an under-14 player in 2018. He had some experience of the role, spending almost half an hour at right-back in a 2-2 pre-season draw with Birmingham City on 31 July.

¡Un #AtletiBarça por todo lo alto en #LALIGAEASPORTS! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/IZy7xJkuad

Fariñas said Flick had asked whether he could play there, and that he felt nervous at first before settling into the game.

The schedule now tightens. Barcelona host Aston Villa in the fourth round of Champions League league-phase games at Spotify Camp Nou on Tuesday 3 November, kicking off at 21:00 local time.

#1274. Fabián Ruiz scores twice as PSG hit Villarreal for six in record-quick start

Paris Saint-Germain scored four goals faster than any side in Champions League history on their way to a 6-0 win at La Cerámica. The defeat leaves Iñigo Pérez taking the blame and Villarreal with one win from four league-phase games.

Fabián Ruiz scored twice as Paris Saint-Germain beat Villarreal 6-0 at the Estadio de la Cerámica on Tuesday 3 November 2026. The visitors led 4-0 at the break in round four of the Champions League league stage.

João Neves opened the scoring in the ninth minute. Désiré Doué added a second three minutes later from a Maghnes Akliouche pass. Senny Mayulu struck in the 13th minute. Ruiz then converted another Akliouche assist.

That fourth goal arrived after 16 minutes and two seconds, beIN SPORTS reported. No team had ever scored four times faster in the competition. By half-time PSG had eight shots on target to Villarreal’s one.

Ruiz added his second in the 50th minute, set up by Vitinha. Flashscore described it as only the second time he had scored twice in a game for PSG. He finished with a rating of 9.81.

David Boly completed the rout in the 78th minute, with Neves providing the assist. The 17-year-old was making his Champions League debut. He scored four minutes after coming off the bench.

The numbers matched the scoreline. PSG completed 677 accurate passes to Villarreal’s 237. Their expected goals reached 2.75 against 0.74. Péter Gulácsi made six saves to keep the margin at six.

Luis Enrique managed this without four regulars. Kvaratskhelia, Dembélé, Nuno Mendes and Marquinhos all missed the trip through injury. The win was PSG’s 10th in a row. It also took them to 14 European Cup matches unbeaten, equalling the longest such run by a French club. After four matchdays, they were the only club in the league phase on 12 points.

Iñigo Pérez left Alberto Moleiro and Georges Mikautadze on the bench. He chose a less attacking line-up than usual. By the sixth goal the stadium was half empty. The fans who stayed whistled the home side again.

Pérez blamed himself for the biggest mistakes. He said his side had got their idea of how to play PSG wrong. He added that they had the wrong mindset after conceding. He also defended Carlos Macià, who had only just turned 18 and faced Vitinha. Pérez put the youngster’s struggles down to his own tactical plan.

At his press conference he would not discuss his own future. He said the squad was devastated and needed to focus on finding solutions.

Villarreal’s European campaign has stalled. They lost 3-2 at Borussia Dortmund on 8 September. A 3-1 home win over Napoli followed on 13 October. They then lost 4-3 at Liverpool on 20 October. Domestically, their previous outing was a 1-0 defeat by Espanyol.

A brilliant performance! 👏❤️💙#VCFPSG 0️⃣-6️⃣ I #UCL pic.twitter.com/6pswWcYZv5

— Paris Saint-Germain (@PSG_English) November 3, 2026

Spain’s other clubs had contrasting nights. Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0 at home. Atlético de Madrid lost 2-0 at home to Bayern München.

Villarreal return to LaLiga at home to Getafe on Sunday 8 November. Their next Champions League match is away to Slavia Praha on Wednesday 25 November, kicking off at 18:45 CET.

#1273. Bournemouth thrash Milan to seal greatest win in club’s history

Eighteen years ago, Bournemouth were minutes away from being liquidated and playing in the fourth tier. On Thursday night, Bournemouth not only welcomed AC Milan in Europe; they did so as favourites, and then pummelled them.

When Amine Adli curled in an 84-minute free-kick with his left foot at the Vitality Stadium, it put the seal on the most extraordinary evening in Bournemouth’s history. On a brutally windy and wet night, Bournemouth trounced AC Milan 3-0.

Amine Adli with a SUPERB free-kick to give Bournemouth a 3-0 lead vs AC Milan 🚀 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/KX5i5oM3TG

Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

The Premier League’s shared riches, allied to years of astute recruitment and management, have underpinned the Bournemouth’s ascent. Even Andoni Iraola’s departure has not stalled the progress at the Vitality Stadium; Marco Rose has relished the new European adventure.

Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz had already been toppled in Bournemouth’s first two European games. Now, Bournemouth have won their first three matches in Europe. Despite middling Premier League form, Rose’s ambitions will extend far beyond securing a berth in the knockout stages of the Europa League. On this evidence, Bournemouth are legitimate contenders to win the competition, and earn a berth in next season’s Champions League.

“It’s a special night for the club,” Ryan Christie, Bournemouth captain, said. “It’s mega – in terms of the story of the club, it’s ridiculous.”

Evanilson, perhaps, was Bournemouth’s standout player against AC Milan, combining intricate linkup play with a constant threat in front of goal. Centre-back Antonio Silva, controlling play from deep while marauding forward, also possessed a calmness that any of Milan’s beleaguered team lacked.

His side’s fate swiftly sealed, Amorim did not bother to summon Luka Modric or Christian Pulisic. Bournemouth’s own bench showed the depth that the club now possesses. Rayan showed off his trickery and directness; Adli – a substitute for substitute Alex Toth, who suffered a hamstring injury – then ensured that Bournemouth secured the margin of victory that their dominance deserved.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.

#1271. Valverde’s stoppage-time strike completes Real Madrid comeback at AEK for 12 points from 12

Substitute captain Federico Valverde struck in stoppage time as Real Madrid twice came from behind to beat AEK Athens 3-2. The win keeps Mourinho's side perfect in the league phase and takes them past his qualification target, days before a trip to Valencia without Vinícius.

Federico Valverde came off the bench in Athens and settled a match Real Madrid had trailed twice. The captain’s long-range strike arrived in the second minute of stoppage time. It completed another away comeback in this Champions League campaign. Mourinho’s side remain perfect after four matchdays.

AEK struck first. Koita put the hosts ahead in the 12th minute. Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside after a review just before the half-hour. He did not have to wait long. In the 32nd minute he equalised with a backheel from Cucurella’s cross.

AEK went ahead again with 15 minutes of normal time left. Stavros Pilios ran onto a pass from Koita and shot through Courtois’s legs. Madrid answered in less than three minutes. Denzel Dumfries played a low ball across goal and Mbappé made it 2-2.

The night ended badly for Koita. AEK’s opening scorer was sent off at 90+5, after the final whistle. He had kept protesting to the referee despite repeated warnings.

The winner carried extra weight given Valverde’s recent fitness. He felt strong discomfort in his right hamstring in the 23rd minute of the 2-1 Clásico win at Camp Nou. Mourinho said afterwards that Valverde had played more than 40 minutes injured. In Athens he started on the bench, yet still had the final say.

Madrid’s European record now reads four wins from four. They beat Inter 2-1 at home, came back to win 4-3 at Roma and beat Leipzig 4-1 at home before this trip. Their tally of 12 points takes them past the 11–12 point mark Mourinho set as the target for qualification. The next aim is a top-eight finish.

The pattern is notable. Both the Roma and AEK wins came after Madrid had fallen behind away from home. In Athens they had to respond on two separate occasions.

Attention now turns to LaLiga, where Madrid remain without Vinícius. On 16 October, the RFEF Appeals Committee rejected the club’s appeal and upheld his ban. Two games were for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair against Villarreal. The other two were for confronting the referee afterwards.

Bellingham // Gyökeres // Aguilar // Valverde ⚽

Four special goals, which was the best? @Heineken | #UCLGOTD pic.twitter.com/KtPJGSRG8C

— UEFA Champions League (@ChampionsLeague) November 4, 2026

The suspension covered the league games against Sevilla, Barcelona and Racing. The last of the four matches is at Valencia’s Mestalla on 7 November, three days after the win in Athens.

Europe then returns. Madrid host PSV on Tuesday 24 November at 9pm CET. They then travel to Arsenal on Wednesday 9 December.

#1269. Lamine Yamal takes Mbappé’s Champions League under-20 scoring record as Barça beat Villa 3-0

Lamine Yamal became the Champions League's top scorer before the age of 20 as Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0, taking the mark from Kylian Mbappé. The record comes soon after Mbappé's double decided the Clásico, and the win lifts Barça to second in the league phase.

Lamine Yamal has taken a Champions League scoring record from Kylian Mbappé. He opened the scoring in Barcelona’s win over Aston Villa at Spotify Camp Nou on 3 November. A Villa mistake in the seventh minute gave him the chance. Yamal curled the ball past goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. That goal was his 14th in the competition. No player has scored more before turning 20. Mbappé had managed 13 at that age. The Real Madrid forward now has 72 Champions League goals in total.

The timing gives the record an edge. Mbappé scored in the 41st and 87th minutes as Real Madrid won the season’s first Clásico 2-1 at Spotify Camp Nou on 25 October. Raphinha’s 61st-minute goal was Barcelona’s only reply that night.

Yamal needed 37 Champions League appearances to reach his total. He does not turn 20 until next July. The record could therefore grow further this season. The two forwards had been level at an earlier stage, each with 10 Champions League goals before their 19th birthdays, according to FC Barcelona.

Raphinha did the rest against Villa. He made it 2-0 in the 52nd minute and struck again 12 minutes later. His double moved him alongside Ronaldinho in Barça’s scoring list. It also lifted his tally for the season to 19 goals in 13 games. The club’s match report named him MVP. Goalkeeper Joan García was picked out as the standout player of the first half.

The result matters for the table as much as the record books. Barcelona came into the game after a 4-2 defeat to PSG. A clean sheet and three goals restored some calm.

The win also ended Villa’s perfect start. The English side had won all three of their earlier league-phase games. This was their first Champions League defeat of the season. Aston Villa said it was their first meeting with Barcelona since their two-legged Super Cup win in January 1983.

Barcelona now sit second. Only PSG, with four wins from four, are above them. Villa have the same points total but trail on goal difference. The league phase runs until 27 January 2027.

Italy are expected to start Pio Esposito, Sandro Tonali, Riccardo Calafiori and Michael Kayode in the penultimate Nations League match, while France rely on Michael Olise in the absence of Kylian Mbappé.

It kicks off at San Siro, the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza in Milan, on Thursday at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

Only the top two go through from Group A1 into the quarter-finals of the Nations League, and currently France lead on 10 points, followed by Italy with seven and Belgium on six.

The final round will see the Azzurri and Red Devils go head-to-head in Brussels, while France host rock bottom Turkiye.

Roberto Mancini is expected to adopt his usual 4-3-3 formation, but there are quite a few doubts over the starting XI.

Brentford right-back Kayode would seem to have done enough to earn his spot, while Arsenal’s Calafiori at left-back means dropping Inter man Federico Dimarco to the bench.

An alternative would be moving Calafiori to central defence with Alessandro Bastoni, therefore starting Dimarco and sending Giorgio Scalvini to the touchline.

In midfield, Davide Frattesi and Tonali seem sure of their places, with Nicolò Barella of Inter the favourite to complete the trio.

Inter striker Pio Esposito is set to lead the attack, but the rest of the trident is up in the air.

His older brother Sebastiano Esposito is the primary candidate on the right side ahead of Como’s Mattia Liberali, while Nicolò Cambiaghi of Bologna would seem to be ahead of Luca Koleosho on the left.

France go into this match without Real Madrid striker Mbappé due to a hamstring injury, and curiously he was also absent when these two teams drew 1-1 in Paris on October 2.

He isn’t the only one, as they have had to give up on Marcus Thuram, Pierre Kalulu, Aurelien Tchouameni, Manu Koné, William Saliba, Jules Koundé, Maxence Lacroix, Ousmane Dembélé, Maghnes Akliouche and Esteban Lepaul.

It is therefore likely that the front three will be made up of Olise, Désiré Doué and Bradley Barcola, but in which order remains to be seen.

Barcola was not originally included to be a centre-forward, but might have to adapt in the circumstances.

If not, then Eli Junior Kroupi or 20-year-old late addition Senny Mayulu could be wild card alternatives to start as Number 9.

There is Serie A representation from Milan pair Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot, while Como midfielder Lucas Da Cunha is expected to start, although Eduardo Camavinga is waiting in the wings.

In defence, Adrien Truffert of Bournemouth is the favourite over Inter’s Andy Diouf for left-back, with either Ibrahim Konaté or Jérémy Jacquet in central defence.

France (4-3-3): Maignan; Gusto, Konaté, Upamecano, Truffert; Cherki, Da Cunha, Rabiot; Olise, Barcola, Doué

#1267. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

As James Ducker and Sam Dean explore in this piece, a succession of Manchester United managers have admonished their team for a lack of industry and athleticism. A number of factors may be to blame: recruitment errors, paralysing pressure and a bad dressing-room culture among them. It is time to get back to basics.

Michael Carrick is not one of the Premier League’s more loquacious managers but supporters will be interested in what he has to say at his pre-Bournemouth press conference this afternoon.

The Manchester United manager is under severe pressure after a run of no wins in seven games across all competitions, and senior players are talking out of school in post-game interviews.

Just when it appeared a line had been drawn under Lisandro Martinez taking on technical director Jason Wilcox, Bruno Fernandes reached for a petrol can and poured more fuel on the flames.

Speaking after the dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes called out Carrick and his coaching staff for their tactical approach, specifically a reluctance to press opponents aggressively in a man-to-man fashion.

Carrick, by his own very measured standards, delivered a pointed response.

“We actually were half-pressed man to man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that,” he said. “And there’s a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

Their opponents on Sunday are Bournemouth, who after a lean run of results under Marco Rose have just dispatched Sunderland for their first league victory of the season, and the mighty AC Milan in the Europa League.

Things do not get easier for United, who go to Stamford Bridge next weekend before a home game against Aston Villa before the November international break.

Telegraph Sport reported on Thursday that former Bayern Munich and Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann features prominently and is understood to want the job – as does Antonio Conte. United are also tracking Fabian Hurzeler while there is interest in Eddie Howe.

United are currently 13th in the table with seven points from seven games.

#1266. Spain face England decider without Rodri, Olmo and Eric García as three uncapped players called up

Spain go into the Nations League decider for top spot against England without the injured Barcelona trio of Rodri, Dani Olmo and Eric García. Luis de la Fuente has handed first senior call-ups to two Betis players and to Real Madrid academy product Jacobo Ramón.

Víctor Muñoz is the fourth player ruled out through injury. Spain arrive in form. They came from behind to win 2-1 in Croatia on 6 October, with Mikel Merino scoring both goals. That made it 11 wins in a row. England beat Czechia 3-0 on the same night, with Harry Kane scoring twice.

Valles, 29, will compete for a place in goal. He has played every minute for Betis this season: 11 league games and all four of their games in the top European competition. Roca turns 30 on 26 November, and his call-up follows a long run of injuries. Jacobo Ramón, the third newcomer, plays in defence for Como and came through the Real Madrid academy.

Valles is one of four goalkeepers in the group. Barcelona’s Joan García is also back between the posts after injury kept him out of the previous squad. Pedro Porro, Nico Williams and Ferran Torres return for the same reason.

Pablo Barrios of Atlético and Ander Barrenetxea of Real Sociedad are also recalled.

Some familiar names are missing for other reasons. Marcos Llorente is absent because he has retired from international football.

The absences in midfield are the most striking. Without Rodri and Olmo, the call for Roca gives De la Fuente another option in the centre of the pitch. Pedri and Fermín are both included.

Several of the squad will be in action on Sunday before joining up. Atlético host Barcelona at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano on Sunday 8 November at 21:00. It is LaLiga matchday 12.

The game carries real weight at the top of the table. Barcelona lead the league on 30 points. Atlético have won their last seven league matches and can go top with an eighth.

#1265. The nine major strategic blunders Ineos have made at Man United that prove they cannot be trusted to choose Michael Carrick's replacement

Published: 21:00 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 13:20 EST, 11 November 2026

Michael Carrick looks set to pay for Manchester United’s miserable start to the season with his job this week – but removing him won't fix the club's deep-seated problems.

Carrick took more points than any other Premier League manager between his arrival as Ruben Amorim's interim replacement in January and the end of last season.

He was rewarded with the job on a permanent basis but the Carrick era has quickly unravelled and United entered the November international break 18th in the Premier League, out of the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle and middling at best in the Champions League.

Carrick's dismissal is the latest shameful episode for Ineos, who took control of football decisions in February 2024 when Sir Jim Ratcliffe came on board as a minority owner.

Daily Mail Sport understands CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox still retain Ratcliffe's backing despite being the subject of fan chants calling for their dismissal at recent matches.

Berrada and Wilcox have failed time and time again and yet seem to escape accountability. Here are nine Ineos mistakes that have dragged Manchester United into the unlikeliest of relegation battles – and raise the question of whether they should be trusted to get the next managerial appointment right.

Michael Carrick's dismissal is the latest shameful episode for Ineos, who took control of football decisions in February 2024 when Sir Jim Ratcliffe came on board as a minority owner

Carrick looks set to pay for Manchester United’s miserable start to the season with his job this week – but removing him won't fix the club's deep-seated problems

Erik ten Hag looked to be on thin ice from the moment Ineos walked through the doors at Carrington.

One of his first conversations with the new hierarchy saw the Dutchman offer to put together a plan to overhaul United’s failing data department. The offer was rejected.

‘I offered my knowledge and abilities to Ineos to help them to construct, but they were of the opinion that they already knew everything,’ Ten Hag told The Athletic recently. ‘They were convinced of, say, the philosophy, the strategy, the work methods. But they came from petrochemicals, from Formula 1, from cycling. Top football demands something totally different.’

That summer, Ineos were caught on the hop by the groundswell of support to keep Ten Hag after United beat rivals City in the FA Cup final, when all indications were they had been ready to sack him. Ineos were put in an awkward spot. That said, they still openly flirted with other managers just days after United’s Wembley victory.

Future England boss Thomas Tuchel met with Ratcliffe in Monaco before he dropped out of the race. Gareth Southgate, Mauricio Pochettino, Thomas Frank and Roberto De Zerbi were considered as Ten Hag remained in limbo, all while United navigated the situation without a sporting director or a CEO.

In the end, with tail between legs, an Ineos delegation flew to Ibiza to interrupt Ten Hag’s holiday and agreed to extend his contract by a year, make changes to his coaching staff, as well as make promises for the upcoming transfer market.

Ineos were caught on the hop and kept on Erik ten Hag (right) after United beat rivals City in the FA Cup final, when all indications were they had been ready to sack him

‘They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned,’ Ten Hag explained. ‘We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn’t keep.’

According to Ten Hag, Ineos went back on their word having said they would not sell Scott McTominay, who joined Napoli that summer for £27.5million, and the manager was sacked 116 days after his deal was extended with another £200m splurged in the transfer window.

By the time Ten Hag was finally dismissed, with a compensation package of £10.4m for him and his coaching staff, Ineos had wasted close to a quarter of a billion through indecision.

Ratcliffe relentlessly pursued Dan Ashworth as he sought an elite sporting director to lead the new sporting structure. He believed the Englishman to be ‘clearly one of the top sporting directors in the world’ and ‘a very capable person’.

Ashworth spent five months on gardening leave after United eventually agreed a near-£3m compensation package with Newcastle United to get him, only to be gone after five months in the North West.

Ratcliffe would go on to blame Ashworth for the decision to stick with Ten Hag and there was a sense that Ashworth was not on board with the move to bring Ruben Amorim in. It all culminated in his shock exit after a 3-2 home defeat by Nottingham Forest in which he was escorted through the press room at Old Trafford with his head bowed en route to a meeting where he was sacked.

Ashworth was paraded as a move that showed Ineos could deliver on their ‘best in class’ mantra, only for them to ditch him embarrassingly quickly.

Dan Ashworth (second right) was paraded as a move that showed Ineos could deliver on their ‘best in class’ mantra, only to embarrassingly ditch him less than six months later

Sir Dave Brailsford, one of Ratcliffe’s most trusted lieutenants, was also an unmitigated disaster. He started off as a crucial figure behind the scenes and his ‘marginal gains’ mantra became a key focus for everyone as he led the renovation of the Carrington training base.

Brailsford drove the appointments of Omar Berrada and Dan Ashworth, and was one of the key men behind ‘Mission 21’, United's bid to win a 21st Premier League title, and ‘Mission 1’, to win a first Women’s Super League title. Both fell under the ‘Project 150’ umbrella he was particularly proud of, to win titles in the club’s 150th anniversary in 2028.

Sixteen months after coming in, Brailsford was removed from day-to-day operations and earlier this year he fully separated from the club by coming off the board.

Brailsford ran football operations at a time of mass redundancies, fans being alienated by ownership, a failing team that produced its worst Premier League finish of 15th, and millions wasted in the transfer market on players that quickly depreciated in value.

Ruthless job cuts, something key Ineos figures have long insisted were essential for the health of the football club, totally destroyed morale and have, according to some remaining staff, completely changed the club for the worse.

In July 2024, staff were told of the need to cut 250 jobs, as company credit cards were cancelled, and staff were asked to contribute towards expenses. In February 2025, Ineos announced a further 150-200 jobs would need to be cut all while austerity measures – the scrapping of free lunches among them – escalated.

All of this against the backdrop of the senior executives continuing to be paid handsomely for gross levels of under-performance.

Having arrived as a technical director working under Ashworth, Wilcox soon found himself thrust into the biggest executive job in the Premier League, as director of football at United.

Omar Berrada (right) is a close friend and supporter of Jason Wilcox (left) and trusts him implicitly, as does Ratcliffe, who believes he has the ‘best eyes’ at the club

He pitched up at United having navigated close to nine months in the same role at Championship side Southampton. Prior to that his expertise had been across at Manchester City in youth development.

Berrada is a close friend and supporter of Wilcox and trusts him implicitly, as does Ratcliffe, who believes he has the ‘best eyes’ at the club. Wilcox was one of the driving forces behind the appointment of Amorim and it was he who would go on to clash with the Portuguese at the end, leading to his eventual sacking.

Wilcox is very hands-on, routinely seen close to training sessions, and has travelled with the team on numerous occasions.

‘When I listen to Jason speak, I get what he’s saying,’ Ratcliffe told The Times in March 2025. ‘He’s a warm character, he’s got a sense of humour, he knows what he’s talking about.’

Wilcox has been accused of interfering too much while not establishing the game model Ineos long promised to implement, regardless of who the head coach is. The director of football was called out in a post-match interview by Lisandro Martinez this season and Wilcox has inexplicably remained in the shadows while players and Carrick face up to the club’s failings.

A patchy recruitment record, all while preparing to search for a third permanent manager in less than 12 months, Wilcox has had next to no positive impact on United’s first team since assuming Ashworth’s job.

Hurting from the way they totally miscalculated and mishandled the Ten Hag situation, Berrada and Wilcox pushed to convince Amorim to abandon Sporting Lisbon mid-season – something he did not want to do – and bring his philosophy to Old Trafford.

It was explained that his 3-4-2-1 system would take a long time to embed onto a squad that had been playing 4-2-3-1 but United's decision-makers were undeterred and forked out £11m to get Amorim and his staff in.

It was explained that Ruben Amorim's 3-4-2-1 system would take a long time to embed but United chiefs were undeterred and forked out £11m to get Amorim and his staff in

A further £250m was spent on the squad the next summer but Amorim's standing took another pounding following a League Cup giantkilling at Grimsby Town

Hiring Amorim in isolation wasn’t an error. He represented a bright young manager that had a clear philosophy – something Ineos haven’t shown in two and a half years – but he had been overlooked by West Ham and Liverpool.

One well-placed source told Daily Mail Sport that Liverpool compiled a dossier on all the reasons Amorim would not be able to succeed at Anfield, largely down to how many players would need to be recruited to make his vision a successful reality.

Amorim was ‘rewarded’ with just two arrivals in January 2025 in the shape of Patrick Dorgu and Ayden Heaven, while the following summer saw a clash of ideas in terms of transfer targets. Senne Lammens arrived despite Amorim seeking a veteran goalkeeper to replace the hapless Andre Onana.

Amorim guided United to their lowest Premier League finish and lost the Europa League final in Bilbao to Ange Postecoglou’s Tottenham Hotspur. A further £250m was spent on the squad with the attack overhauled but his standing took another pounding following a League Cup giantkilling at Grimsby Town.

Relations between Amorim and Wilcox deteriorated severely and they clashed in a meeting on the eve of the trip to Leeds United, which would prove his final game. Amorim unleashed a fierce rant which intimated that figures such as Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell were overstepping the mark with their input and that they needed to allow him to be the ‘manager’ of the club.

Having come under pressure to change formation and the style of play, Amorim was sacked the morning after drawing at Leeds.

Rather than actually devise a plan to deliver Amorim’s vision, Ineos instead tried to get clever and turned to Harry Marra, a renowned track and field coach, to come in as a consultant.

He was given the remit of assessing individual player running mechanics, acceleration and deceleration. Mason Mount was one of those who Marra identified and he attempted to adjust the 36-cap England midfielder’s running gait.

Ratcliffe imparted advice on stretching techniques he had learned from running the London Marathon to figures in the Carrington physio room

Add from the episode in which Ratcliffe imparted advice on stretching techniques he had learned from running the London Marathon to figures in the Carrington physio room, you got the picture of an ownership that didn’t seem to understand that top-level football isn’t track, field, or cycling.

Performance on the pitch only got worse after this, not better.

8. Prioritising new stadium over a new left back

Speaking to reporters in Dublin this summer shortly after being given the United job full-time, Carrick used the word ‘push’ almost a dozen times when referencing what the club still had to do in the transfer market.

But Ineos, again believing they are the smartest people in the room, ignored those pleas and stuck to their plan to ‘fix’ one part of the team per summer. It was the attack in 2025, and in 2026 it would be the midfield, with the defence to come next year.

So, despite knowing full well that expecting another injury-free campaign from Luke Shaw was an enormous gamble, they did it anyway and made no defensive reinforcements. It hasn’t taken long for that move to backfire spectacularly.

Instead, the decision was made to purchase land to the tune of £60m so they can plough on with plans for a swanky new 100,000-seat 'Wembley of the North' stadium that many fans believe will never be built.

Rather than fixing the team's defence, United chiefs spent £60m on a slither of land to progress with their plans for a 100,000-seat 'Wembley of the North'

The way Carrick has been treated in this whole saga has been cruel and a sign of why managers should think twice about taking a job under Ineos

An emergency meeting after a 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth last month looked set to be the end for Carrick until Berrada, Wilcox, Ratcliffe and the Glazers surprised the football world and simply did nothing. Everyone just continued with business as usual with no backing for the beleaguered Carrick.

Defeat at Chelsea, coupled with two frantic displays to come from 2-0 down against both Roma and Aston Villa followed. Then came the revelation on Monday that Berrada and Wilcox had settled on a recommendation to the board that they should sack Carrick. But instead of being sanctioned immediately, Carrick spent seven hours at Carrington on Tuesday to take training and watch an Under 17s match.

We are told yet again that Carrick's future will finally be decided on Wednesday at a meeting in Monaco, but in the meantime he must carry on until he gets wind he has been officially sacked.

The way Carrick has been treated in this whole saga has been cruel and a sign of just why managers should – and will – think twice about taking a job under Ineos.

#1264. Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity1,2,3,4,5. We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells)6. Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by Nr3c1) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 (Rgs2), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal–immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

Functional cellular heterogeneity is well documented in hepatocytes, driven by liver zonation7, and in muscle fibres, shaped by local environmental cues, particularly motor neuron activity8. Single-cell technologies have revealed extensive new patterns of heterogeneity of specific cell types within the same tissue9, yet their biological importance remains largely undetermined.

Thermogenic adipose tissue undergoes adaptive thermogenesis and is crucial for energy expenditure and thermoregulation1,2. Its specialized metabolism and precise responses to environmental and physiological stimuli make it an ideal model for studying functional cellular heterogeneity. Thermogenic capacity declines substantially with age in rodents and humans, leading to age-related cold sensitivity and metabolic disorders3,4,5, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

BAs and beige adipocytes mediate UCP1-dependent non-shivering thermogenesis10. Although substantial progress has been made in identifying the key pathways that activate thermogenesis, most studies have been conducted at the whole-tissue level, leaving the mechanisms governing its activation, maintenance and deactivation incompletely understood.

The heterogeneity of BAs within the same brown adipose tissue (BAT) and beige adipocyte cluster within inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT) has been characterized by our group6 and others5,11,12,13,14. We found that BAs heterogeneously express UCP1 and classified those with low expression as BA-L cells and those with high expression as BA-H cells6. At room temperature, BA-H cells constitute 30–50% of all BAs; BA-H cells predominate after cold exposure, whereas BA-L cells predominate under thermoneutral conditions6. This raises questions of why BA heterogeneity exists, and whether it reflects random variation along a thermogenic continuum or spatially organized, tightly regulated states within the tissue.

Here we identify dynamic bistable regulation of BA heterogeneity controlled by the spatial proximity of BAs to IL-1β puncta through a neuronal–immune regulatory mechanism. This regulation becomes dysfunctional during ageing, leading to cold intolerance in older adults. These findings highlight how different cell types collectively control cellular heterogeneity in a spatiotemporal manner, integrating environmental and internal cues to regulate tissue metabolism and function.

Reanalysis of our previous single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset6 revealed enrichment of glucocorticoid signalling and GR-target genes in BA-L cells (Extended Data Fig. 1a–c). Top BA-L-cell-enriched genes include H6pd, Rgs2 and thioredoxin-interacting protein (Txnip), whereas BA-H cells were enriched for thermogenesis-related genes, including Ucp1 and cytochrome c oxidase 6B1 (Cox6b1) (Extended Data Fig. 1a,b,d–f). Nr3c1 was similarly expressed in BA-H and BA-L cells (Extended Data Fig. 1e,f).

We generated Ucp1-Chaser-mT/mG mice for inducible labelling of Ucp1+ cells by crossing the Ucp1-rtTA, TRE-cre and Rosa-stop-mT/mG mouse lines (Extended Data Fig. 2a). After 1 week of feeding on a doxycycline diet at room temperature (24 °C), GFP+ and GFP− BAs showed a patchy distribution (Fig. 1a), consistent with BA heterogeneity in AdipoChaser mice6. The Ucp1-rtTA mice used a relatively weak 5 kb Ucp1 promoter15 so GFP is only expressed in UCP1high-expressing BAs (BA-H cells), while Ucp1-cre mice have a strong bacterial artificial chromosome-based Ucp1 promoter that drives Cre expression in all BAs16. Immunofluorescence (IF) staining confirmed selective H6PD expression in BA-L cells (Fig. 1a); 50% of BAs were UCP1+(GFP+)H6PD−, 45% were UCP1−(GFP−)H6PD+ and 5% were UCP1+(GFP+)H6PD+ (Fig. 1b). Similar heterogeneity was observed in iWAT after 1 week of cold exposure (6 °C) (Fig. 1c), with 45% of these beige adipocytes being UCP1+H6PD−, 49% UCP1−H6PD+ and 6% UCP1+H6PD+ (Fig. 1d). Human BAT showed a similar reciprocal UCP1 and H6PD pattern in multilocular brown–beige adipocytes (Fig. 1e), 45% of BAs were UCP1+H6PD−, 47% were UCP1−H6PD+ and 8% were UCP1+H6PD+ (Fig. 1f). Western blotting confirmed more than twofold higher H6PD in BA-L cells than in BA-H cells and more than fourfold higher UCP1 in BA-H cells than in BA-L cells, while H6PD was enriched in mature BAs relative to in the stromal vascular fractions (SVFs) (Extended Data Fig. 2b,c). Together, these data identify H6PD as a BA-L marker.

a,b, Male Ucp1-Chaser-mT/mG mice (aged 10 weeks) were fed a doxycycline chow diet for 1 week at 24 °C. Representative images of BAT IF staining for GFP (green), H6PD (red), perilipin (white) and DAPI (blue) (a), and quantification of the relative percentage of BAs positive for GFP+(UCP1+) only, H6PD+ only or both (b). n = 6 per group. c,d, Male Ucp1-Chaser-mT/mG mice aged 10 weeks were fed a doxycycline chow diet for 3 days or 1 week at 6 °C. c, Representative images of IF staining for GFP (green), H6PD (red) and DAPI (blue) in iWAT. d, Quantification of the relative percentage of BAs positive for GFP+(UCP1+) only, H6PD+ only or both. n = 4 per group. e, Representative IF staining for UCP1 (green), H6PD (red), perilipin (white) and DAPI (blue) in human supraclavicular BAT. f, Quantification of the relative percentage of BAs that are positive for UCP1+ only, H6PD+ only or both. n = 5 per group. g, BAs differentiated from primary BAT SVFs from WT mice were reverse-transfected with H6pd Dicer-substrate small interfering RNAs (dsiRNAs) or control dsiRNAs and collected after 2 days. RT–qPCR analysis of H6pd, Rgs2, Hsd11b1 and Ucp1 mRNA levels. n = 3 per group. h–j, 10-week-old male Ucp1-mGFP mice were injected with lentivirus overexpressing H6PD or mCherry as a control into BAT. h, After 2 weeks, H6PD and β-actin protein levels were analysed using western blotting (WB). i, Representative IF staining of BAT for GFP (green), perilipin (red) and DAPI (blue). j, Quantification of the BA-H cell percentage. For j, n = 5 (mCherry) and n = 4 (H6PD). Statistics were computed using one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey’s multiple-comparison test (b, d and f), unpaired two-tailed Welch’s t-tests (g (H6pd and Hsd11b1)) or unpaired two-tailed Student’s t-tests (g (Rgs2 and Ucp1) and j); *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ****P < 0.0001. For b, d, f, g and j, data are mean ± s.e.m. Scale bars, 25 μm (a (right), c (bottom)), 50 μm (a (left), c (top) and e) and 100 μm (i).

To enable real-time labelling of BA-H cells, we generated Ucp1-mGFP knock-in mice by inserting a P2A-mGFP cassette after Ucp1 exon 6, immediately upstream of the stop codon (Extended Data Fig. 2d). These mice displayed robust BAT GFP fluorescence without altered UCP1 expression (Extended Data Fig. 2e,f). GFP IF staining revealed a heterogeneous distribution of GFP+ and GFP− BAs (Extended Data Fig. 2g). In vitro-cultured BAs and beige adipocytes showed selective H6PD expression in GFP− BA-L cells (Extended Data Fig. 2h), validating our in vivo findings.

We next investigated UCP1-independent thermogenesis through the futile creatine cycle17,18,19,20,21. Tissue-non-specific alkaline phosphatase (TNAP) and creatine kinase B (CKB) protein levels increased 4.8-fold and 2.5-fold, respectively, in BAT during cold exposure and were enriched 2.9-fold and 2.0-fold in BA-L cells versus in BA-H cells (Extended Data Fig. 3a,b), consistent with higher Ckb mRNA in BA-L cells6. IF staining further showed TNAP enrichment in BA-L cells (H6PDhigh BAs) in BAT and H6PDhigh beige adipocytes in cold-exposed iWAT (Extended Data Fig. 3c,d). In vitro-differentiated BAs also displayed selective TNAP expression in BA-L cells (GFP− BAs) (Extended Data Fig. 3e), indicating that the futile creatine cycle is more active in BA-L cells.

Regarding the metabolic differences between BA-L cells and BA-H cells, BA-L cells have half the basal respiration, but similar maximal respiration compared to BA-H cells, indicating similarly high mitochondrial potential6. Using in vivo [U-13C]glucose tracing22, we recently showed that BAT has the most active glucose oxidation among metabolically active tissues, while in vitro tracing confirmed active glucose oxidation in differentiated BAs23. To characterize BA-L metabolism, we performed [U-13C] glucose and [U-13C] palmitate tracing in freshly isolated BA-H cells and BA-L cells, followed by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) analysis (Extended Data Fig. 4a). Fully labelled (m+16) free palmitate (C16:0) was about twofold higher in BA-L cells, indicating greater fatty acid uptake (Extended Data Fig. 4b), while fully labelled total palmitate was sixfold higher, suggesting preferential fatty acids storage in BA-L cells (Extended Data Fig. 4c). BA-L cells also showed lower citrate enrichment from both tracers, indicating lower glucose and fatty acid oxidation (Extended Data Fig. 4d). Thus, BA-L cells exhibit greater fatty acid uptake and accumulation but lower fatty acid and glucose oxidation, consistent with their lower basal respiration6.

We next examined whether H6PD is a functional marker of BA-L cells. H6PD depletion in BAs differentiated from BAT SVFs of Ucp1-mGFP mice increased Ucp1 expression sixfold (Fig. 1g), indicating that H6PD negatively regulates Ucp1. Conversely, H6pd overexpression by lentiviral injection into BAT of Ucp1-mGFP mice (Fig. 1h and Extended Data Fig. 4e,f) significantly reduced the proportion of BA-H cells (Fig. 1i,j). Thus, H6PD is a functional marker of BA-L that regulates UCP1 expression and BA heterogeneity.

H6PD localizes to the endoplasmic reticulum lumen and generates endoplasmic reticulum-resident NADPH, distinct from cytosolic glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD)24. H6PD primarily determines the reductase activity of endoplasmic reticulum-localized 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (HSD11B1), which converts inactive cortisone to active cortisol25. GR protein levels were similar between BA-H cells and BA-L cells, indicating that GR signalling is not regulated by receptor abundance (Extended Data Fig. 3b). We next investigated whether GR signalling regulates UCP1 expression. Simultaneous treatment of BAs differentiated from the SVFs of wild-type (WT) mice with 11-dehydrocorticosterone (11-DHC), a natural substrate for active glucocorticoid biosynthesis25, and noradrenaline (NA) substantially increased UCP1 protein (Fig. 2a). However, 24 h 11-DHC pretreatment blunted NA-induced UCP1 expression (Fig. 2b). Thus, prolonged activation of GR signalling suppresses BA responsiveness to NA, maintaining BA-L cells in a stable, low-thermogenic status.

a–c, BAs differentiated from primary BAT SVFs of WT mice were treated with NA ± 11-DHC for 24 h (a) or pretreated with vehicle or 11-DHC for 24 h, followed by NA (b) or forskolin (c) treatment for 24 h. UCP1 and β-actin immunoblots and quantification. n = 3 independent cultures.
